To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we introduce a novel model for extractive question answering, (2) our model outperforms previous state-of-the-art results, and (3) our model is efficient and can be used in real-world applications.
we present a novel model architecture for answer extraction in question answering, and we show that it improves upon the best previous result on the SQuAD dataset.

we propose a model for extractive question answering that uses a recurrent span encoder to produce fixed length representations of spans, that we show that this approach outperforms the state of the art by 5% absolute, and that this approach decreases the error of a baseline model by >50%.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can we efficiently represent all spans of a given document in order to answer a question? Can we use the span representations to improve answer extraction? Can we use these span representations to improve question answering performance?

1) we propose a novel neural architecture that builds fixed length span representations for all possible answer spans; 2) our model outperforms other approaches that factor prediction into separate word or start/end predictions; 3) our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on SQuAD, improving over the previous best by 5%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
explicit span representation is an effective way to model the answer in a reading comprehension task.
the span extraction task is not a simple task of identifying start and end markers, but rather requires the ability to predict the entire span at once.
explicit span representations are a useful intermediate representation that is amenable to learning with a recurrent neural network.
